- Cost: $0.074 per landed promotion (token cost at real DeepSeek pricing).
- 60 human checkpoints ever, all answered: reject 52, approve 7, continue 1. Median raise-to-decision 1,326 s; gate checkpoints 261 s.

Each node is a claim someone could act on, with the *mechanism* included. Do NOT write "X is important" or "Y has challenges". Write what was measured, in what population, with what number, and what the design tension was. # Your assignment: w9-verifier-judge

Topic: what a verifier can and cannot certify, and whether a model judge can be calibrated without human labels.

The gap queue of this graph ordered these questions by how many other nodes depend on the answer. Answering one is worth more than adding five new claims that nothing depends on.

* ver-q02: Can model-based grading be calibrated cheaply? Published agreement numbers disagree wildly (some report kappa >0.8, others near 0).
* gap-w4-033: Can a judge be calibrated against test outcomes alone, no human labels, and still predict the axes tests cannot see?
* gap-w4-036: Is there ANY published case of a self-improving coding loop reverting a promoted harness change after the fact?
* orch-016: Does adaptive K (more candidates when a verifier is uncertain) survive a verifier that is only as good as the task's own test command?

Direction: a loop whose score IS the task's test command has no independent yardstick. Find what the literature actually establishes about (a) judge-vs-test agreement measured on real code patches, with the numbers and sample sizes, (b) calibration without labels (weak supervision, agreement triage, conformal prediction on judges), (c) documented cases of a judge preferring a patch that the tests reject or vice versa. Pay attention to whether reported agreement is measured on the same distribution the judge is used on -- distribution shift is the usual hole. For (c) also look for revert/remediation records in self-improving systems (DGM, AlphaEvolve, SICA, Darwin Godel Machine replications) and any audit of promoted changes later found harmful.

Write to `C:\Projects\RSI\research\\wave9\\w9-verifier-judge.json`. Aim for 20-30 nodes, 20-35 edges, 6-9 gaps. Work for as long as it takes to read the primary sources; do not stop at abstracts.
